experiment: Universality test: Ising vs Heisenberg inter-chain coupling
verdict: WITHDRAWN. Both Hamiltonians produce a rise-then-fall correlation curve, but the curves are different shapes: they peak at different couplings and fail a scaling-collapse test at chi2/dof = 9.0 with the worst point 4.1 sigma off. The r = 0.89 reflects the shared shape family, not shared physics. What survives is that both couplings produce a cross-field signal well above shot noise.

superseded.reason: curve_correlation was a bare Pearson r on 8 points with no interval, no null distribution and no goodness-of-fit test. Both sweeps rise from zero, peak and fall, and unrelated unimodal curves with a randomly placed peak reach r = 0.89 about 16% of the time, so the value is close to the baseline expectation for any two curves of that shape.

scaling_collapse.note: Fits a shared shape with per-Hamiltonian amplitude and coupling scale. Near 1 would mean the curves are the same shape to within shot noise. The test accepts 84% of genuinely universal pairs, so it is not simply strict.
